finding.claim: GET /invoice/<inv_id> returns any invoice to any caller with no authentication and no ownership check (missing authz / BOLA-IDOR).
finding.source: inv_id path parameter, fully attacker-controlled; the request needs no session or credentials.
finding.sink: INVOICES.get(inv_id) -> jsonify(inv) at lines 9-10 (protected operation: reading another customer's invoice record).

trace.note: Route registered with no auth decorator.
get_invoice(inv_id) takes the ID straight from the URL.
Looked up in global INVOICES dict by attacker-supplied key; no check that the record belongs to the caller.
Entire invoice dict serialized and returned.

finding.guards_checked: No @login_required or equivalent on the route; no before_request hook in this file; no ownership comparison (contrast /my/invoice at line 16, which has one); no per-route policy. The only mitigating possibility is a global before_request in the wider app that enforces login, which is not in the reviewed code. Even if it exists, this endpoint still lacks any object-level check, so any logged-in customer can read any invoice. If no global guard exists, it is fully unauthenticated.

verdict.guard_found: None on the route. invoices.py:7 has no auth decorator, and there is no before_request hook in the file (the only file in the directory). The only other control is an unseen app-wide before_request, which would not add an object-level check. The ownership check at invoices.py:16-17 exists only on /my/invoice, not on get_invoice.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches invoices.py:7-10: the route at line 7 has no auth, line 9 returns INVOICES.get(inv_id) with no ownership comparison, and line 10 serializes the whole record, so any logged-in customer can read any invoice (BOLA), which confirms the core claim. The "fully anonymous" part is not verifiable from this directory, because g.user at invoices.py:16 implies an unseen auth layer that may or may not gate this route.

finding.claim: Ownership checks compare inv['customer'] to g.user['id'] without ensuring g.user['id'] is set. If an anonymous or unauthenticated user object has id None and an invoice has customer None (unassigned), the check passes and the invoice is returned. The same precondition applies to /my/invoices at line 23.
finding.source: g.user['id'] (set by code outside this file) and the stored invoice's 'customer' field (data-dependent).
finding.sink: Ownership comparison at line 16 gating jsonify(inv) at line 18, and the list filter at line 23 returning all matching invoices.

trace.note: get_my_invoice reads g.user, which is set outside this file.
Equality check against g.user['id']; passes if both are None (or both equal).
list_mine filters with the same comparison, so every invoice whose customer is None is returned to an anonymous caller.

finding.guards_checked: Abort(404) on a missing invoice (line 15), so this only matters for existing records. The check fails closed if g is missing user (AttributeError -> 500) or if g.user has no 'id' key (KeyError), so those cases are not bypasses. No explicit guard rejects a None user id or None customer. Confidence is low and depends on the auth middleware and the data model, neither of which is in the reviewed code. Confirm whether g.user can be anonymous with id None and whether invoices with customer None can exist.

verdict.guard_found: None in invoices.py. The only control is abort(404) on a missing invoice at invoices.py:15, which does not test ownership. The ownership comparison at invoices.py:16 and the list filter at invoices.py:23 have no None check.
verdict.reason: The line references in the trace match invoices.py:15, 16, 18 and 23, but the note on line 14 is wrong: that line is the def, and g.user is first read at line 16. Whether this is exploitable depends on facts outside this file: whether g.user can be anonymous with id None (set by middleware not in the repo) and whether invoices with customer None can exist in INVOICES (populated elsewhere). Both are unknown here, so the finding can be neither confirmed nor refuted from the code available.
